name: Ibuprofen
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: 400 mg every 4 to 6 hours as needed (higher single doses no more effective)
1,200 to 3,200 mg/day (400, 600 or 800 mg three or four times daily); maximum 3,200 mg/day

key_interactions.effect: Less blood-pressure and diuretic effect; risk of acute kidney injury (label); hyperkalemia, especially in older, volume-depleted or CKD patients (NSAID class labeling).
key_interactions.action: Avoid the triple combination where possible; if used, check creatinine and potassium within 1 to 2 weeks and keep the patient hydrated.

key_interactions.effect: Higher risk of serious bleeding (label: warfarin, aspirin; SSRIs and SNRIs: NSAID class labeling).
key_interactions.action: Avoid if possible; otherwise monitor for bleeding.

key_interactions.effect: More gastrointestinal toxicity without added benefit (label).

key_interactions.action: Monitor drug levels and kidney function.

key_interactions.effect: More nephrotoxicity with cyclosporine; higher digoxin levels (NSAID class labeling).
Ibuprofen can block aspirin's antiplatelet effect (label).
key_interactions.action: Give immediate-release low-dose aspirin at least 2 hours before once-daily ibuprofen; not shown for enteric-coated aspirin (label).

common: Gastrointestinal complaints (4% to 16% in trials), e.g., nausea, epigastric pain, heartburn
serious: Acute kidney injury, papillary necrosis; hyperkalemia (NSAID class labeling)

contraindications: Asthma, urticaria or allergic-type reaction after aspirin or other NSAIDs
Setting of coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery
monitoring: Serum creatinine and potassium at baseline and during use in CKD, heart failure, cirrhosis, older adults, or with ACE inhibitors, ARBs or diuretics
Blood pressure; signs of gastrointestinal bleeding; hemoglobin if anemia symptoms

pk.metabolism: Hepatic oxidation to inactive metabolites A and B
pk.excretion_renal_pct: 45% to 79% of dose in urine within 24 hours (metabolites); about 1% free drug
